title: Layer a rubric by concern
statement: Keep a rubric's format rules apart from its subject, curriculum and grade specifics, and supply the standard's text at evaluation time rather than writing it into the rubric.
detail: Changes to the evaluator's prompts took grade-level standard codes and difficulty calibration out of a format overlay, assessment-specific framing out of two item-type prompts, and one course's unit and practice names out of a prompt, since those arrive at evaluation time from the curriculum source. The rules stated with them: type overlays hold format-specific behaviour only, grade and curriculum specifics belong in curriculum-subject overlays, item types are described the same way whatever the assessment, and hard-coding standard text is an anti-pattern. No measurement comes with these changes.
against: A newer rubric breaks the rule by naming one grade's science authority in the prompt itself: '**Authority for G7 Science:** NGSS standards and standard middle school science curricula (state frameworks, widely used textbooks).' (shadow-bench/src/inceptbench/prompts/video_script/evaluation.txt line 160).

evidence.quote: The AP Chemistry unit names and science-practice names are curriculum content that is injected at evaluation time via the curriculum context (incept-curriculum API). Hard-coding the taxonomy in the prompt is the "no hard-coded standard text" anti-pattern.
Type overlays must hold format-specific behavior only; grade/curriculum specifics belong in curriculum-subject overlays.
The evaluation methodology is the same regardless of assessment (STAAR, MAP, etc.) — item types should be described generically.
curriculum-specific guidance belongs in curriculum overlays, not type overlays per the prompt-layering rule
